figures.shows: Block diagram of the three types of classical KD. A teacher model (Layer 1 to Layer n) and a student model receive the same input data. The teacher's and student's intermediate representations (t1..tn, s1..sn) are compared in feature-based distillation. Teacher logits (Z_T) and student logits (Z_S) pass through temperature-scaled softmax (P_T, P_S) into response-based distillation. Relation structures between the representations feed relation-based distillation. No numeric values.
figures.confirmed_by: The knowledge transferred through KD is commonly grouped into three categories [1], as illustrated in Fig. 1:

figures.shows: A two-by-two matrix of teacher model (classical, quantum) against student model (classical, quantum): classical to classical (conventional KD), classical to quantum, quantum to classical, quantum to quantum. The last three cells are shaded as the configurations the survey covers. No numeric values.
figures.confirmed_by: In general, the teacher-student interaction results in four distinct combinations, as shown

figures.shows: Pipeline for classical-to-quantum response-based KD. A classical teacher model produces logits Z_T, then temperature-scaled softmax P_T. A quantum student circuit (|0> inputs, repeated U blocks) is measured; the measurement probabilities go directly to the student distribution, or through a classical mapping and temperature-scaled softmax P_S. Teacher and student distributions are compared for distillation; a task loss on ground-truth labels joins the total loss. No numeric values.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 3 summarizes a representative classical-to-quantum response-based distillation pipeline followed by many distillation frameworks.

figures.shows: Checkmark table comparing three existing KD surveys and this work on six columns: Tutorial, Classical KD, Quantum KD, Quantum-inspired, Applications, Benchmarking. The three prior surveys cover classical KD, applications and (fully or partly) benchmarking, and do not cover tutorial, quantum KD or quantum-inspired KD. This work is marked as covering all columns, with classical KD partially covered.

papers.what_it_is: A survey and tutorial of quantum knowledge distillation (classical-to-quantum, quantum-to-quantum, quantum-to-classical, quantum-enhanced and quantum-inspired) with a taxonomy, application review, benchmarking critique and open problems, covering 33 studies in its taxonomy tables.

assertions.value: The authors state that the survey covers studies of knowledge distillation that involve quantum or hybrid quantum-classical models, or quantum resources incorporated into the distillation process.
quotes: This survey covers studies on knowledge distillation involving quantum or hybrid quantum-classical models, or quantum resources incorporated into the distillation process.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Section I.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum transfer learning and quantum-state distillation are distinct from knowledge distillation and are not typically included in the survey, unless they explicitly involve a teacher-student distillation objective.
quotes: Related approaches such as quantum transfer learning and quantum-state distillation are distinct from knowledge distillation and are not typically included
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own inclusion limits in Section I.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose a multidimensional taxonomy for quantum KD, classifying studies by teacher-student configuration, quantum model type, transferred knowledge and optimization goal.
quotes: We propose a multidimensional taxonomy for quantum KD, classifying studies by teacher-student configuration (classical-to-quantum, quantum-to-quantum, and quantum-to-classical), quantum model type, transferred knowledge, and optimization goal
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own contribution and scope in Section I.A.

assertions.value: The authors state that existing KD surveys primarily focus on KD of classical models and do not consider quantum or hybrid models as either teachers or students.
quotes: they primarily focus on KD of classical models and do not consider quantum or hybrid models as either teachers or students.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim about other surveys, not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum KD as a knowledge distillation framework in which the teacher, the student, or both involve quantum or hybrid quantum-classical models.
quotes: Quantum KD is generally defined as a knowledge distillation framework in which the teacher, the student, or both involve quantum or hybrid
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the definition it uses in Section III.A.

assertions.value: The authors state that the teacher-student interaction gives four combinations: classical-to-classical, classical-to-quantum, quantum-to-quantum and quantum-to-classical KD, where classical-to-classical is conventional KD.
quotes: classical-to-classical (C2C), classical-to-quantum (C2Q), quantum-to-quantum (Q2Q), and quantum-to-classical (Q2C) KD.
Classical-to-classical distillation corresponds to conventional KD.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own taxonomy in Section III.A.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum-enhanced distillation as a complementary category in which quantum resources are used within the distillation mechanism, while the teacher and the student are classical networks.
quotes: quantum-enhanced distillation is a complementary category in which quantum resources are used within the distillation mechanism, while the teacher and the student are classical networks.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the definition it uses in Section III.A.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum-inspired KD as teacher-student transfer performed entirely on classical hardware, in which the teacher, the student or the distillation mechanism uses a quantum-derived mathematical construction, without evaluating any quantum state, circuit or kernel at any stage.
quotes: Quantum-inspired KD is a conceptually distinct category that denotes the teacher-student transfer performed entirely on classical hardware
without evaluating any quantum state, circuit, or kernel at any stage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the definition it uses in Section IV.E.

assertions.value: The authors state that offline distillation is particularly prevalent in quantum KD settings, where a pre-trained classical teacher is most commonly frozen and later used to guide the student model.
quotes: This training scheme is particularly prevalent in quantum KD settings, where a pre-trained classical teacher is most commonly frozen
assertions.certainty_reason: An author characterization of the literature, with no count given.

assertions.value: The authors state that setting alpha = 0 reduces the combined objective to standard supervised training with no distillation signal, and that setting alpha = 1 removes the ground-truth supervision so the student trains only on the distillation loss.
quotes: Setting α = 0 reduces the objective to standard supervised training with no distillation signal
whereas setting α = 1 removes the groundtruth supervision, training the student only on the distillation loss.
assertions.certainty_reason: A definitional consequence of the objective the paper writes in Section II.C.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tau-squared term compensates for the reduction in gradient magnitude introduced by temperature scaling.
quotes: The τ 2 term compensates for the reduction in gradient magnitude introduced by temperature scaling
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper attributes the argument to the original distillation work.

assertions.value: The authors state that in quantum or hybrid models the features used for alignment may include classical activations or estimated expectation values of quantum observables, and that access to the full quantum state is not generally assumed.
quotes: In quantum or hybrid models, features used for alignment may include classical activations or estimated expectation values of quantum observables; access to the full quantum state is not generally assumed.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement of a modeling assumption, without derivation.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for classification, the class probability is obtained by summing the probabilities of the measurement outcomes assigned to the class, and that KL(p_T || p_S) without temperature scaling applies provided both distributions refer to the same classes and the student assigns positive probability wherever the teacher does.
quotes: the class probability is obtained by summing the probabilities of the outcomes assigned to it.
provided both distributions refer to the same classes and the student assigns positive probability wherever the teacher does.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement of method with its conditions, not a proved theorem; the statement is quoted from the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that for Pauli observables with expectation values in [−1, 1], the range of probability distributions that temperature-scaled softmax of those values can represent is limited, and they give an upper bound on the probability of any class.
quotes: However, for Pauli observables with oj ∈ [−1, 1], the range
of probability distributions that can be represented is limited.
assertions.certainty_reason: The bound itself is an equation (Eq. 14) that the text layer prints in pieces, so the full statement could not be quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: Read from Figure-like equation on p.7: the bound is e^(2/tau) / (e^(2/tau) + C - 1), checked by eye on the page image.

assertions.value: The authors state that the conventional tau-squared argument does not automatically transfer to a quantum student whose measurement probabilities come from Born's rule, and that in that case tau-squared may still be used but should be read as a selected loss weight rather than a gradient correction.
quotes: This argument does not automatically transfer to a quantum student whose measurement
should be interpreted as a selected loss weight rather than a gradient correction.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author argument without derivation in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is essential to report whether the temperature is applied only to the teacher, to a classical readout of the student, or to both outputs.

assertions.certainty_reason: An author recommendation on reporting practice.
